_meta.name: l2o-ci-hygiene
_meta.notes: CI-hygiene wave on zai/glm-5.3 workers. KNOWN-ISSUES.md has 7 sections; local verification shows most are already FIXED but the CI gates masking them (continue-on-error) are still in place. Each task retires one mask + its section. Parallel builtin workers; ci.yml hunks are textually distinct per task.

tasks.title: Flip lint-rust to required: verify clippy clean, retire rustfmt debt
steps: VERIFY FIRST: (a) cargo fmt --all -- --check (already rc=0 locally), (b) cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings from server/ — if clippy flags anything, FIX the flagged code in the owning crate (minimal fixes, no refactors) before proceeding.
Remove `continue-on-error: true` from the lint-rust job (ci.yml ~line 23) and delete the KNOWN-ISSUES comment block above it.

docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md §4 (rustfmt/clippy debt): replace the section body with a one-line resolution note: 'RESOLVED <date>: rustfmt debt fixed; lint-rust now required (no continue-on-error). Commit <sha>.'

Verify: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; /usr/bin/python3 -c "import yaml,sys; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/ci.yml')); print('yaml ok')" (if pyyaml missing: /usr/bin/python3 -c "import json" fails — instead check with ruby or just visual diff; the step is a sanity check, skip if no yaml lib).
Commit ONLY .github/workflows/ci.yml and docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md.
tasks.accept: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && cargo fmt --all -- --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

tasks.title: Fix acroform doctest, make workspace doc tests required
steps: The acroform.rs doc example (line ~9) fails to compile: `pdf_bytes` is not defined. Fix the example honestly: mark it ```no_run AND define `let pdf_bytes: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();` (or a minimal valid setup that compiles). Do NOT delete the example. If PdfiumBackend::new() would panic at doc-test runtime locally, no_run is REQUIRED.
Verify: cargo test -p wo-pdf-render --doc (must be fully green, 0 failed).

Then run cargo test --workspace --doc from server/ — if EVERY crate's doc tests pass (this is the CI 'Run doc tests' step), remove `continue-on-error: true` from that step (ci.yml ~line 127). If some OTHER crate's doctests also fail, fix those too (same standard: make compile/pass, minimal edits) — then flip.
docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md: if §5 (wo-ooxml roundtrip) — VERIFY cargo test -p wo-ooxml --lib passes locally (it does as of 2026-11-07) and mark §5 RESOLVED with date.
Verify: cargo test --workspace --doc
Commit ONLY the listed files.

tasks.title: Fix shift-enter-behavior.test.mjs ES-module import
steps: The test fails: 'ReferenceError: require is not defined in ES module scope'. Convert any require() calls to ESM import statements (readFileSync from node:fs, etc. — mirror how label-parity.test.mjs does it). Keep the test's assertions intact.
Verify: /usr/bin/node --test shift-enter-behavior.test.mjs passes AND the neighbors stay green: /usr/bin/node --test label-parity.test.mjs ctx-menu.test.mjs shift-enter-behavior.test.mjs
Commit ONLY the one listed file.

tasks.title: Pdfium runtime guard in wo-pdf-render tests, make coverage-rust required
steps: ROOT CAUSE: build.rs downloads pdfium but it never lands on the CI runtime loader path; tests that call PdfiumBackend::new().expect(...) PANIC instead of skipping. Add a small guard helper (e.g. pub(crate) fn pdfium_available() -> bool in renderer.rs using catch_unwind or a backend init probe) and convert the panicking .expect() test setups to: `if !pdfium_available() { eprintln!("skipping: pdfium unavailable"); return; }` across wo-pdf-render tests. Do NOT weaken real assertions — only the availability precondition.
Verify locally: cargo test -p wo-pdf-render --lib (must stay green; pdfium IS available locally so the skip path just compiles). Also cargo test -p wo-pdf-render --doc stays green.
Remove `continue-on-error: true` from the coverage-rust job (ci.yml ~line 172) and the KNOWN-ISSUES comment above it.
docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md §2 (pdfium guard): mark RESOLVED with date.
Verify: cargo test -p wo-pdf-render --lib && cargo test -p wo-pdf-render --doc
Commit ONLY the listed files.
tasks.accept: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && cargo test -p wo-pdf-render --lib && cargo test -p wo-pdf-render --doc

tasks.title: KNOWN-ISSUES sweep: verify + mark sections 1, 3, 6 statuses
steps: §1 wo-x2t-wasm uuid wasm build: the WASM Build workflow has been GREEN on recent pushes (e.g. 38dfe0d9d). Verify via: gh run list --workflow=wasm.yml --limit 3 (or gh run list --limit 6 and filter). If all recent wasm runs are success, mark §1 RESOLVED (the uuid feature issue no longer reproduces). If actually red, FIX it instead: add uuid features = ['js'] to core/crates/wo-x2t-wasm/Cargo.toml and keep §1 open with the fix noted.
§3 ocis SSE: already marked HISTORICAL — no change needed beyond confirming.
§6 Biome: already marked resolved — confirm.
§7 docker.yml wasm-pack: check .github/workflows/docker.yml + recent runs of that workflow; if green, mark resolved; if the file doesn't exist, mark OBSOLETE (workflow removed).
Update the 'How to clear these' cheat sheet at the bottom to reflect the new state (after L2O-01/02/04 also land, most sections are resolved — write it as of the actual current state).
Verify: docs parse as clean markdown; any gh checks you ran are pasted in the commit message.
Commit ONLY docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md (and Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock IF §1 needed a fix).
